item.title: Third Chicago CFO’s Surprise Exit Sparks Credit Rating Fears
item.description: Chicago has lost its third chief financial officer this year, raising concerns about the city’s credit ratings as it scrambles to close an $882 million budget deficit.

item.title: The Billion-Dollar Business of Virtual Schools
item.description: US online public schools are enrolling more students than they did during the pandemic, and nowhere has the expansion happened faster than in Texas. But what does this trend mean for the education students receive? (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: K-Beauty Boom Becomes Wall Street’s Latest Investment Play
item.description: Korean beauty products have long filled American medicine cabinets. Now, a new exchange-traded fund is set to test whether there’s room for them in US investors’ portfolios as well.

item.title: Compass Sues Multiple Listing Services, Upping Antitrust Row
item.description: A feud over how consumers can buy and sell homes escalated on Thursday with a slew of antitrust lawsuits filed across the country by the top US broker for residential properties.

item.title: Dollar Poised for Best Week in Over a Month on Fed Hike Bets
item.description: The dollar is heading for its strongest weekly advance in more than a month, extending a rally fueled by growing expectations that the Federal Reserve will increase interest rates next month.
